kubernetes-networking-under-the-hood.r: Calls to an external API took five seconds, but only from pods, because ndots:5 made the resolver try several cluster search suffixes first. Ending the name with a dot fixed it.
kubernetes-networking-under-the-hood.x: Read the endpoints, then the labels, then DNS. Most Kubernetes network problems are one of those three.

cni-network-policy-and-ebpf.r: A security review found a database reachable from every namespace even though a NetworkPolicy existed, because the cluster ran Flannel, which does not enforce policy at all.
cni-network-policy-and-ebpf.x: Pick a CNI that enforces policy, observe traffic first, allow DNS, add allows before default deny, and test that blocked traffic is really blocked.

what-a-service-mesh-is-and-how-it-works.r: After a control plane upgrade some proxies stayed on old config and returned 503s. Rolling the upgrade slowly and checking proxy-status avoided it later.
what-a-service-mesh-is-and-how-it-works.x: Adopt a mesh for a specific need, restart workloads after enabling injection, check proxy-status, and roll upgrades slowly.

mtls-and-traffic-management.r: Retries at three layers turned a slow database into a full storefront outage, because each user request became dozens of calls. Limiting retries to one layer and adding outlier detection fixed it.
mtls-and-traffic-management.x: Migrate with PERMISSIVE then STRICT, create DestinationRules before VirtualServices, run istioctl analyze, and keep retries at one layer.

observing-and-troubleshooting-the-mesh.r: Checkout failed even though every pod was Running, because 40 proxies were STALE after the control plane ran out of memory. istioctl proxy-status found the cause in seconds.
observing-and-troubleshooting-the-mesh.x: Check config sync first, read the flag, check endpoints and policies, and run more than one control plane replica.
